Question Choices: Fill: A model is built from non-overlapping unit cubes, each with a volume of 1 cubic unit. Only 6 cubes are visible from the front. After checking the entire model, you confirm that it contains exactly 9 cubes in total. The volume is __ cubic units.
Hints: Use the confirmed total number of cubes, including hidden cubes. Multiply by the volume of one cube.
Solution: The complete model contains 9 cubes, and each has volume 1 cubic unit. Total volume = 9 x 1 = 9 cubic units. The 6 cubes visible from the front are only part of the model, so that visible count alone does not give the volume.

Question Choices: Fill: Area is measured in square units. Volume is measured in __ units
Hints: Volume uses cubic units. Choose the size of unit to suit the object.
Solution: Area uses square units, formed from two lengths. Volume uses cubic units, formed from three lengths.

Question Choices: Select which unit is best for measuring the volume of a small die: ~~cubic-meters | square-centimeters | cubic-centimeters~~
Hints: Volume uses cubic units. Choose the size of unit to suit the object.
Solution: A small die has a small three-dimensional volume, suitably measured in cubic centimetres. Square centimetres measure area; cubic metres are too large a practical unit here.

Question Choices: An object has 4 layers and 5 cubes in each layer. Each cube is 3 cubic centimeters. The volume of this object is __ cubic centimeters
Hints: Multiply layers by blocks per layer, then by the volume of each block.
Solution: 4 layers × 5 cubes per layer = 20 cubes. Each has volume 3 cubic centimeters, so total volume = 20 × 3 = 60 cubic centimeters.

Question Choices: A small cooler is filled completely with 14 ice bricks. Each brick is exactly 1 cubic foot in size. What is the total volume of the cooler? __ cubic feet
Hints: Multiply the number of blocks by the volume of one block.
Solution: 14 blocks × 1 cubic feet per block = 14 cubic feet. Count every block once; these blocks fill the solid without gaps.
